title: Cash Application Rules for Premium Billing Accounts
content:
**Rule of application.**

> **Former clause — no longer in force in its general form:** "A payment is applied to the oldest unpaid coverage month first."
> This continues for every payment, other than the following: at the grace-cure payment of an individual-market account in a grace period, an earlier grace-cure payment by check or bank transfer that is still inside its clearing hold is applied to the oldest unpaid coverage month only once it clears, and is not counted toward the grace-cure payment. Every other payment is applied to the oldest unpaid coverage month first.

**Paid-through date.** The paid-through date advances only by whole coverage months fully paid.

> **Former clause — no longer in force in its general form:** "A month counts as fully paid when the amount applied to it reaches the payment threshold percentage of its net premium."
> This continues for every payment other than the renewal payment of a Cascade Individual Annual Prepay account whose renewal invoice is corrected under the renewal payment rules; for that payment only, a renewal month counts as fully paid when the amount applied to it reaches the payment threshold percentage of its premium as corrected. For every other payment a month counts as fully paid when the amount applied to it reaches the payment threshold percentage of its net premium.

On a group account a month also counts as fully paid when the amount applied falls short by no more than the group underpayment tolerance. Any shortfall carries forward as balance.

**Effects of a payment.**
- A payment for the binder (the first billing period) moves a pending-binder account to active.
- A payment that brings every past-due month to fully paid during a grace period cures the grace period.
- A payment received after a lapse is applied as a reinstatement payment only when the reinstatement rules allow it, and is otherwise refunded.
- Payments that would pay more than the arrangement's months payable in advance are refunded for the excess.

**Accepted methods.** A payment is accepted only by a method in the arrangement's accepted payment methods; binder and reinstatement payments only by the stricter binder payment methods and reinstatement payment methods.

**Past-due premium.** The premium past due is the sum of the net premium due for the coverage months from the month after the paid-through date through the current month — the invoiced amounts less the payments and credits applied to them.

**Hypothetical illustration.** A Cascade Individual Direct Bill Monthly account with a net premium of 61.00 a month and two unpaid months receives 100.00: the oldest month receives 61.00 and is fully paid, so the paid-through date advances by one month; the second month receives 39.00, is not fully paid, and its 22.00 shortfall carries forward as balance.

superseded_clauses: A payment is applied to the oldest unpaid coverage month first
a month counts as fully paid when the amount applied to it reaches premium_payment_threshold_pct of its net premium
